sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 10.05.2022 at about 6.00 pm., the petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider on two wheeler bearing No.KA- 42-L-4752, when they reached near to Bogaiah Land,
Tumbenahalli Village, Kailancha Hobli, Ramangara Tq & Dist.
At that time, the rider of the motor cycle rode the same in high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.4172/2022 left the two wheeler in a road ditch.
Due to which petitioner lost his control and fell down from the two wheeler and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Narayan Hospital, wherein surgery was conducted.
Thereafter he was shifted to KIMS Hospital for higher treatment.

The petitioner has spent more than Rs.4,00,000/-
towards treatment, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as agriculturist and also running dairy farming and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
The petitioner has lost his earning capacity and cannot do his normal work prior to the accident.
The accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Hero Honda Passion Pro Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-42-L-4752.
The jurisdictional Police have registered a Criminal Case against the rider of the motor cycle in Cr.No.161/2022 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
After (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.4172/2022 investigation the Police have filed Charge Sheet against the rider of motor cycle.
The respondents being Owner and Insurer of the motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, petitioner constrained to file a petition for compensation.
3. After service of notice the respondent No.1 did not appeared before the Court and was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is as under:
This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of Hero Honda Passion Pro Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-42-L-4752 and liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and subject to valid and effective driving license of the rider.
This respondent has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
It has specifically denied the manner of (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.4172/2022 accident, the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.

It has also denied the injuries sustained, treatment taken and expenses incurred towards Mohan Kumar vs Prakash T.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17588961/
2 medicine.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
With this ground it has prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that on 10.05.2022 at about 6.00 pm., while he was proceeding as a pillion rider in two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA-42-L-4752 near Bogaiah Land, Tumbenahalli Village, Kailancha Hobli, Ramanagara, at that time the rider of the two wheeler came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the left side of the road ditch.
Due to impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries in the alleged RTA?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum of compensation?

from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and got marked document at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10, Dr.Nagaraja B.N was examined as PW2 and got marked document at Ex.P11 & 12.
The 2 nd respondent did not choose to adduce its evidence.
6. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner.
The learned counsel for 2 nd respondent has filed written arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

7. My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2: In the Affirmative;
Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
-:R E A S O N S:-
8. Issue No.1:- It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 10.05.2022 at about 6.00 p.m., the petitioner met with an accident due to rash and negligent (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.4172/2022 riding of rider of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-L-4752 while petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider and due to impact petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

3 9.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination by reiterating all the facts mentioned in the petition.
He also relied documents at Ex.P1 to P10.

The Ex.P1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the wound certificate, Ex.P3 is the FIR, Ex.P4 is the complaint, Ex.P5 is the Charge Sheet, Ex.P6 is the wound certificate, Ex.P7 is the IMV Report, Ex.P8 is the Mahazar,
Ex.P9 is the discharge summary and Ex.P10 is the medical bills.
10. A perusal of above records it shows that shows that one Nagaraju S/o.

Late Mote Gowda who is the father of petitioner has lodged First Information before Ramanagara Rural Police Station on dated 11.05.2022 alleging that on 10.05.2022 at about 5.00 pm., his son herein petitioner met with an accident due to rash and (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.4172/2022 negligent riding of rider of vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-L- 4752 while petitioner was proceeding as a pillion rider and due to impact petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
On the basis of this first Information the Ramanagara Rural Police have registered the case in Cr.No.161/2022 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 & 337 of IPC.

Thereafter, the Investigating Officer had conducted the Investigation and filed the Charge Sheet against the rider of the motor cycle by name Prakash.T.N., herein 1st respondent i.e., owner of the motor cycle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 & 338 of IPC.
11.
The PW1/petitioner has stated the cause of the accident in his chief-examination affidavit.
The PW1 was subjected to cross-examined but nothing was elicited to disbelieve the evidence of PW1 with regard to accident.

The Respondent No.2 though contended that the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-L-4752 vehicle was not involved in the accident but showing this aspect the (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.4172/2022 respondent No.2 has not led any evidence.
Moreover the Ex.P7 MV Report discloses that the some parts of motor cycle was damaged.
The 2nd respondent only denied the case of the petitioner.

Apart from this in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal case.

This principles of law was laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others).
12.
The learned counsel for the 2 nd respondent tried to elicited in the cross-examination of PW1 that there is one day delay in lodging the complaint.
Since the injured has sustained severe injuries and as such we cannot expect to lodge the complaint by the injured soon after the accident.

Normally, injured person will give preference to take treatment rather than compliance of (SCCH-9)
10 MVC.No.4172/2022 legal requirements.
Same has been done by the petitioner in this case.
Therefore, the question of delay losses its significance.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in a reported decision (2011) 4 SCC 693 Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that - " It is well settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian Conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after the accident.

Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of the kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated Mohan Kumar vs Prakash T.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17588961/
4 rather than to rush to the Police Station.

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay the Courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so, the contents of FIR should (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.4172/2022 also be scrutinized more carefully.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons, then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the Police to initiate investigation of Criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves the factum of accident, so that victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay is doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

Therefore, the documents relied by petitioner and oral evidence of PW1 clearly establishes that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence act of the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-L-4752.
Now it can safely be concluded, that the injuries were caused to the petitioner due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending vehicle.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved issue (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.4172/2022 No.1.
Hence, I answered issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant, charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.

let me discuss one by one:
a) TOWARDS INJURY, PAIN AND SUFFERING: the petitioner has contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and discharged with an advise to take follow up treatment.

In order to prove injuries caused to him he has produced wound certificate/Ex.P2, which reveals that petitioner has sustained injuries and doctor has opined that the petitioner (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.4172/2022 sustained grievous injury.
The record also shows that the petitioner took treatment in the hospital as an inpatient and the petitioner has examined doctor by name Dr.Nagaraj.B.N as PW2 to prove the disability.
The PW2 got marked documents at Ex.P11 & 12.
The PW.2 has assessed the disability of petitioner.
Therefore by considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.30,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at hospital and produced medical bills marked at Ex.P10 for Rs.2,48,769/-.
The learned counsel for 2nd respondent while cross-examination of PW1 suggested that only Rs.2,43,560/- was spent.
This suggestion is goes to show that the respondent No.2 is admitting medical expenses of (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.4172/2022 Rs.2,43,560/- and not Rs.5,00,000/-.
The petitioner claiming medical bill amounting to R.2,48,769/-.
The 2 nd respondent admitted Rs.2,43,560/- and as per Ex.P10 the bill amount is for Mohan Kumar vs Prakash T.N on 15 April, 2024

5 Rs.2,48,769/-.
Further there is no serious dispute about these medical bills.
Hence the Tribunal is of the view that petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,48,769/- is just and reasonable towards medical expenses.

c) TOWARDS FOOD, EXTRA NOURISHMENT, AND MEDICAL ATTENDANT CHARGES: on perusal of the records it shows that the petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Narayana Hospital as well as KIMS Hospital from 10.05.2022 to 11.05.2022, from 11.05.2022 to 20.06.2022 and from 29.06.2022 to 30.06.2022 respectively i.e., for a period of 43 days.
During the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 43 (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.4172/2022 days to a sum of Rs.43,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra nourishment and medical attendant.
d) TOWARDS CONVEYANCE:
According to petitioner, he spent some amount for conveyance while he was admitted in the hospital till discharge from the hospital.
It is true that the petitioner has not produced any document to show he has incurred expenses for conveyance.
However, it is quite natural that if any person admitted in the hospital he might have spent some amount towards conveyance.

Therefore,
considering the injuries and treatment taken by the petitioner this tribunal is of the opinion that Rs.10,000/- is just and proper towards conveyance charges.
e) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner contended that he is an agriculturist and also doing dairy farming and earning Rs.25,000/-pm, as a salary.
In order to prove his income he has not produced any documents to show that he was (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.4172/2022 earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income this Tribunal will consider notional income.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2022 at 15,500/- p.m.

For determination of income before Lokadalath for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka,
Principal Benches, Bengaluru.

So in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2022 treated as Rs.15,500/- p.m., as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case this tribunal held that petitioner is entitled to Rs.62,000/- = (Rs.15,500/- x 4) towards loss of income during laid up period.
f) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.4172/2022 contended that due to accident he was inpatient in the hospital and has become permanently disabled.
The petitioner also examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N working as an Orthopeadic Surgeon, at Sai Ortho & Dental Centre, Bengaluru as PW2.
This PW2 deposed that petitioner came to their hospital with history of RTA and sustained Comminuted fracture of the right proximal tibia.

Mohan Kumar vs Prakash T.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17588961/
6
As per wound certificate ExP6 the doctor has opined that the injury No.1, 3 are grievous in nature and Injury No.2 & 4 are simple in nature.
The PW2/Doctor has assessed the physical disability at 46% and to the whole body at 15%.
In order to prove his disability the doctor/PW2 has produced clinical notes and one X-ray film, which are marked at ExP11 & 12 respectively.
It is material to note that during the course of cross-examination there is nothing to elicit from the mouth to disbelieve the evidence of PW.2 about assessment of disability.
The petitioner contended that he was an agriculturist and running dairy (SCCH-9) 18 MVC.No.4172/2022 farm.
But not produced any document to show his avocation.
Therefore mere non producing of documents it cannot be said that the petitioner is not doing any work.
The PW.2 assessed the whole body disability at 15%.
The petitioner sustained injury to the right proximal tibia and underwent surgery.

Therefore considering avocation of the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and considering the evidence of PW.2 and all the aspects available on record the functional disability is assessed at 15%.
In order to prove the age of the petitioner he has not produced any document.
However, as per medical records his age was 40 years at the time of accident.
Hence the age of the petitioner is taken into consideration 40 years for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "15" is applicable as per Smt. Sarala Verma's case.
As per the ratio laid down in Raj Kumar V/s Ajay Kumar and anr, this Tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his income.

sentences.text: As already stated above the petitioner has not produced any document to prove his income.
Therefore, in the absence of positive documents about salary the notional income has to be considered.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
15,500 x 12 x M15 x 15%/100 = Rs.4,18,500/- The petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,18,500/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
g) Towards Deprivation Of Future Amenities:
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he can do his work with some difficulties.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.8,000/- is just and reasonable towards under the head of deprivation of future amenities.

h ) F U T U R E M E D I C A L E X P E N S E S : T h e d o c t o r P W 2 ( S C C H - 9 ) 2 0 MVC.No.4172/2022 has opined that the petitioner is required Rs.60,000/- for future medical expenses i.e., for removal of implants in situ.
But the doctor has not produced any estimation cost for the future medical expenses to the petitioner.
The petitioner claiming Rs.1,00,000/- for future medical expenses.

However considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the injuries sustained by the petitioner I am of the view that an amount of Rs.50,000/-
is just and reasonable towards future medical expenses.
14. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

Regarding Liability:
As already stated above the petitioner has proved that the accident in question was caused by the rider of the motor cycle with rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle.
The respondent No.2 has admitted issuance of policy in favour of respondent no.1 in respect to motor cycle but it has contended that the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
As stated above in this case, there is no material to show that the respondent no.1 has violated the policy conditions.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle (SCCH-9) 22 MVC.No.4172/2022 is primarily liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, the tribunal proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .8,70,769/- (Eight Lakhs Seventy Thousand Seven Hundred Sixty Nine Only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of (SCCH-9) 23 MVC.No.4172/2022 one month from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 50% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 50% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper verification an identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
